end.title: One verified science story a day

caption:
The LZ dark matter experiment reported one nuclear recoil event at 248 keV in 2.84 tonne-years of exposure (220 live days). Known backgrounds produce such an event about 0.5% of the time: 2.6 sigma global. Not a discovery. Preprint on arXiv, submitted to Physical Review Letters, 2026, not yet peer-reviewed. What would convince you?

#darkmatter #physics #particlephysics #science
voiceover_script: Dark matter may have just hit a detector. Once. But this is not a discovery. Here is what the LZ experiment reported on the first of September. One event, a nuclear recoil at two hundred and forty eight kilo electron volts, over two hundred and twenty live days and a two point eight four tonne-year exposure. Known backgrounds produce an event like this about half a percent of the time. That is not the chance dark matter is real. It is the chance ordinary physics did this anyway. In sigma: three point four local, two point six global. Far short of a discovery. If it were a WIMP, its mass would be above two hundred G E V. The paper is a preprint, not yet peer-reviewed. Source in the caption.
